Key Research Thinking Patterns: Computational Enhancement of Physical Systems: Using advanced computational techniques to overcome the physical limitations of imaging hardware. (e.g., Applying Fourier Ptychography Microscopy (FPM) to low-magnification lenses (4x, 10x, 20x) to reconstruct high-resolution chromosome images comparable to those from high-magnification (100x) lenses, thus breaking the trade-off between a large field-of-view and high resolution. Also, using a CAD scheme to analyze mammograms to predict the risk of "mammography-occult" tumors missed by standard interpretation).

Cross-Domain AI Adaptation: Identifying and adapting state-of-the-art AI architectures from the general computer vision field to solve specific, challenging medical imaging problems. (e.g., Applying Multi-view Vision Transformers (MVT) to classify breast cancer from unregistered multi-view mammograms, outperforming standard CNNs. Also, employing Virtual Adversarial Training (VAT) to leverage unlabeled data for breast mass classification, addressing data scarcity).

Clinical Workflow Simplification: Designing systems and algorithms that are practical for real-world clinical use by removing complex or time-consuming prerequisites. (e.g., Developing a high-resolution FPM system for chromosome imaging that avoids the need for oil immersion, unlike conventional 100x lenses. Also, creating a Transformer-based CAD scheme that works on "unregistered" mammograms, eliminating the error-prone image registration step).

Comparative Validation against Gold Standards: Systematically validating new methods by objectively comparing their performance against established conventional techniques. (e.g., Quantitatively comparing FPM systems against conventional microscopes using a standard USAF 1951 resolution target and generating Modulation Transfer Function (MTF) curves. Also, assessing new CAD models by comparing their AUC performance against other state-of-the-art CNN models).
Summary Description: Dr. Hong Liu specializes in Electrical and Computer Engineering, with a primary focus on Medical Image Analysis and Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD). His research involves the application and supervision of advanced computational methods, including Deep Learning and Computational Imaging, to address challenges in diagnostic medicine. He oversees projects utilizing Fourier Ptychography Microscopy (FPM) for high-resolution chromosome imaging and the development of deep learning models like Vision Transformers for breast cancer diagnosis from mammograms. His work contributes to creating novel diagnostic tools for oncology and cytogenetics, often involving roles in project administration and funding acquisition.
